newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares turn sour on rate, fx jitters.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares turn sour on rate, fx jitters.

text.p: After a strong opening, Greek shares reversed direction on Thursday on rising interbank rates in reaction to a softer drachma.
The one-month Athibor, the reference rate for Greece's interbank market, firmed 57 basis points to 11.50 percent on Thursday in relation to forex outflows.
Dealers said rates jumped on ecu and mark buying for drachmas and could climb further if forex outflows continued.
Fixed coupon bonds were losing ground for the same reasons, with prices falling 40 to 60 basis points, while FRNs came under less pressure.
Greece's central bank intervened at the fixing to prop up the drachma selling large amounts of ecus and marks.
Equity brokers said the turbulence in Greece's money and forex markets sparked off limited profit-taking by investors who were bound to cash in their stakes sooner or later.
"The rate hike related to the forex turbulence was a good reason for investors riding the rally to take some of these profits," said Thanos Trikatzis, a broker at Hermes Brokerage.
A broker at a major securities house said the downturn was not an unusual event, judging that the market would resume its uptrend.
"These things happen in equity markets and I do not expect today's drop to stop Greek shares from their upward course," said a broker who requested anonomity, adding that "the market will rebound."
Other brokers said OTE was under slight pressure ahead of its upcoming part-float next month.
"I sensed slight but focused selling pressure on OTE from foreign portfolios which are trying to cut a better deal on the forthcoming part-flotation and rights issue," said another broker.
State telecoms OTE will go ahead with a sizeable part-flotation and a rights issue in late June at price terms which will greatly rely on the market prices prevailing at the time.
The Athens general index fell 1.92 percent or 32.94 points to 1,682.88, turning back after a firm start which peaked at 1,729.39.
Except for insurance stocks which posted a 0.46 percent advance, all sectors registered losses.
Banks and industrials lost 2.73 and 1.85 percent, respectively, with construction shedding 1.86 percent.
Turnover grew to 29.5 billion on volume of 6.1 million shares.
Declining stocks beat advancers 168 to 57 with 26 shares unchanged on 251 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,109-1,139. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 70 drachmas to 6,900.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted lower at 698.05-742.60. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $91.33-$93.02. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 4,066-4,298 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $21.32-$23.02. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted lower at 298-332 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
